what Stripe or Plaid do with data after it leaves; what sent payloads contain
PCI scope, access reviews, encryption at rest, network controls, training

assumptions: Stripe and Plaid hosts are api.stripe.com and production.plaid.com; sandbox hosts not approved
Bank account numbers are sensitive and kept out of responses but not forbidden from storage, since the ask names cardholder data
Vendor allowlist applies to all outbound http in the workspace, not only card flows
Recipe's charge_card function not needed: payments/charge already calls Stripe
pci tag name chosen by me; no tag vocabulary exists in the workspace
confusions: Field attribute syntax for sensitive ({sensitive = true} after the type) is not shown in the skill, templates or catalogue; I guessed it and the dry run accepted it
Table tag syntax (tags = [...] inside the table block) is not documented in the kit; inferred from workflow_test files and accepted by dry run
Recipe says datadog.log should be covered alongside debug.log in LOG-001, but the template's own rule is debug.log only; I put datadog.log in PCI-CARD-001
Recipe's build list assumes a new charge_card function; for a workspace whose charge endpoint already calls the processor, the recipe does not say whether to refactor it or leave it
Whether a policy can be built when the existing code already violates it is not addressed: the ask is 'pass the audit' but the policies will report failures today
wished_for: Worked example of a sensitive field and a table tag in XanoScript
Guidance on existing violations when a recipe is applied to a workspace that already breaks it (report vs. fix)
A check for raw storage of named fields that also says which object writes them
why_confidence: Policies parse, dry run is clean, and the enforcement fields are wired in; but they are advisory and currently report real violations (raw card storage, card logging, non-approved vendor). Nothing has been evaluated, and the policies cannot see runtime data or org controls, so they will not by themselves pass a PCI audit.
